4. While the suit was pending in the trial Court the plaintiff filed a petition on 1-3-2000 for holding local investigation by survey knowing Advocate Commissioner for relaying the suit land with the land of title deeds mentioned in the plaint as in those deeds there was no mention of plot number and khatian number, etc as because those deeds were executed and registered long before the SA operation came into being. 

 8. Mr Khijir Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that after filing of the suit in the trial Court, it was detected that there is no mention of plot and khatian in the deeds mentioned in the plaint as the deeds were executed and registered before SA operation; that it is necessary to determine whether the land of deeds in question relates to the suit land for which the plaintiff filed a petition on 1-3-2000 for holding local investigation by an Advocate Commissioner for relaying the suit land with the land of title deeds mentioned in the plaint. He further submits that the defendant in his written statement denied that the deeds of the plaintiffs are not related to suit land but the defendant-respondent admitted to this extent that the suit land could not be properly ascertained and identified without local investigation. 

 12. There is no denying of the facts that there is no mention of dag and khatian in those kabalas referred to in the plaint as those are executed and registered long before the settlement operation. As the defendant No. 2 stated in paragraph 11(Uma) of the written statement that the suit land does not attract the land of those Kabalas, so the plaintiff filed an application on 1-3-2000 under section 75 read with Order XXVI, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for local investigation for the purpose of relaying the suit land and for elucidating the matter in dispute. But the learned Subordinate Judge heard the petition on 14-3-2000 and rejected the same holding that the matter can be resolved by oral evidence. 

 16. In the instant case, it is urgently necessary to ascertain through local investigation whether the land of registered kabala of 1318 BS and the land of registered kabala dated 5th Srabon, 1334 BS, relates to suit land or not. This fact cannot be collected through oral evidence and this matter can only be ascertained through relayment of the land of kabalas stated in the plaint. It is to be ascertained first, whether the land of the kabalas of the plaintiff attracts the suit land or not. Without relayment, such matter cannot be elucidated because there is no mention of plot and khatian in those kabalas referred to in the plaint as those were executed and registered long before the SA operation came into being.
